@@ -27,12 +27,17 @@
 
   Current FucO P0A9S1 is 382 residues, whereas the 2005/2023 papers use historical 383-residue numbering and older
   P11549 context. Their Asp196/His200/His263/His277 Fe ligands, G17D/G97E/D39G, N-terminal deletion and I7L/L8V
-  engineering labels are not silently renumbered onto the current reference. The structure has one Fe site per chain
-  but solution WT Fe occupancy was about 0.53. His267 is not the Fe ligand formerly proposed. N-terminal strand
-  exchange supports the dimer; historical deltaN10 loses assembly/activity. The pQE32/pCM1 His6 preparation in M15(pREP4)
-  differs from pGEX3X/pCM2 in BL21 and its cleaved WT/mutant preparations. Two NAD sites per dimer and D39G cofactor
-  expansion do not create a wild-type NADPH core. Older partially purified mutant enzyme also used added manganese;
-  that preparation-specific alternative is retained.
+  engineering labels are not silently renumbered onto the current reference. The pQE32/pCM1 N-terminal His6 preparation
+  in M15(pREP4) supports the one-Fe-site crystal observation. Separately, solution metal analysis compared D196L/H200A/H200F
+  mutants with WT containing 0.53 Fe atom/subunit. Methods assign WT/mutant site-directed-mutagenesis preparations
+  to pGEX3X/pCM2 in BL21(DE3), with GST removed by factor Xa; this Methods/Results join supports the cleaved-WT
+  comparator attribution, not a measured occupancy for the His6 crystal preparation. His267 is not the Fe ligand
+  formerly proposed. N-terminal strand exchange supports the dimer; historical deltaN10 loses assembly/activity.
+  Two NAD sites per dimer and D39G cofactor expansion do not create a wild-type NADPH core. Older partially purified
+  mutant enzyme also used added manganese; that preparation-specific alternative is retained. The 2005 paper reports
+  earlier Cu(II)/Cd(II) inhibition of FucO, citing PMID4306747. Its retained older-source evidence is abstract/landing
+  material, not an inspected full experimental body; no Cu/Cd dose or direct assay is inferred. The 2005 Figure
+  4 experiment separately tests Zn/Fe.
